title: The {5, 8} funnel
why: Collatz-type largest-prime-factor map; cycle {5,8} confirmed, but excluding divergent prime-driven climbs is Collatz-hard.

title: Doubling minus one
why: Composites shrink, primes double (Cunningham chains of 2nd kind); cycles confirmed; no obvious potential function, Collatz-like.

title: Two long loops
why: Cycles through 46 (9) and 80 (7) confirmed; global convergence of mixed P-map is Collatz-type.

title: Gerver's constant has unbounded partial quotients
why: Unbounded partial quotients unknown even for pi; Gerver's constant is defined implicitly, so this is far out of reach.

title: Three large consecutive factors
why: Needs three consecutive integers each n^0.9-almost-prime; beyond Tao-Teraväinen correlation methods, near parity barrier.

title: A mixed Fermat equation
why: Integral points on a log-general-type surface; no local obstruction found (moduli <400), no small solutions; finiteness needs Vojta-type input.

title: Five squares of seven-free primes
why: Hua five-prime-squares with Maynard digit restriction; quadratic Weyl sums over digit-restricted primes are hard but plausible.

title: Square-sum 4-cycle factors
why: C4-factor of square-sum graph; likely constructive/absorption, Hamiltonicity already known; moderate combinatorics.

title: Additive energy of largest prime factors
why: Weighted p1+p2=p3+p4 with smooth weights Psi(N/p,p): four-variable circle method gives the asymptotic routinely.

title: Cops on square sums
why: Same as existing 'Cops on square sums'.

title: Global convergence of P(n)+P(n+k)
why: If every k works (conjectured), the set is N and trivially recursive; recursiveness of one fixed set is not a meaningful target.

title: Pythagorean triangles of legs
why: Pairwise leg-sums squares = Euler brick; Saunderson's 1740 parametric family gives infinitely many with polynomially bounded c.

title: Prime-sum graph and perfect codes
why: Perfect codes in bipartite prime-sum graph; closed neighbourhoods ~2n/log n force tiny codes; likely only small n, needs sieve care.

title: Spectral radius of the prime-sum graph
why: Every vertex degree is pi(v+2n)-pi(v) ~ 2n/log n uniformly, so lambda_1 ~ 2n/log n, c=2, by min/max degree bounds.

title: Number of square-sum colourings
why: Depends on chi(S_inf), itself open/possibly infinite; degrees grow like sqrt N so the normalisation is unclear.

title: Primes in the {5,8} funnel's tree
why: Positive density of each fate needs distributional control of orbits of P(n)+P(n+1); f(n) small only on density-zero sets.

title: Packing density of Gerver's sofa
why: Packing density of Gerver's sofa is unknown even numerically; proving transcendence is far beyond methods.

title: Two-corner sofa
why: Same as existing 'Zigzag sofa' (right then left turn after distance d).

title: Unit distances in the hat tiling
why: Hat vertices lie in a fixed periodic kite-grid set; unit-distance graph has bounded degree, so the max is Theta(n).

title: Hat tiling Schrödinger operators
why: Same as existing 'Hat spectrum is a Cantor set' / 'Hat electrons'.

title: Rotation-proof lattice-point-poor shapes
why: Second-order term of min-max rotated lattice count runs into Gauss circle problem-type discrepancy; also somewhat vaguely posed.

title: Minimal Steiner tree for prime points
why: Constant c depends on joint distribution of prime gaps (Gallagher/Hardy-Littlewood); upper bound c<=1 trivial via vertical lines.

title: Ising model on the spectre tiling
why: Exact beta_c and SLE3 on aperiodic non-isoradial graph; open even for generic periodic graphs; sibling of existing hat Ising items.

title: Percolation threshold of the square-sum graph
why: Threshold 1/lambda of kernel 1/(2sqrt(x+y)) via inhomogeneous/dense-graph percolation theory; needs local tree-likeness check.

title: Random greedy square-sum path
why: Random greedy path on deterministic graph of degree ~sqrt N; no differential-equation method directly applies; limit may be 0.

title: First-passage percolation on primes
why: Sites with a+b prime are never nearest neighbours (consecutive sums differ in parity), so the restricted graph is disconnected; no shape theorem.

title: Random digit deletion
why: Heuristically c=1 (harmonic sum of prime chances); rigorous needs higher-moment prime counts on digit-deleted numbers.

title: Doubled prime map with a 1231 loop
why: Cycles (93..315) and (1231,2473,6183) confirmed; growth on primes up to 2.5x makes global convergence Collatz-type.

title: Triple factor map minus two
why: Fixed points 8, 33 and cycles through 20 (13), 177 (9) confirmed; global convergence is Collatz-type.

title: The Jacobian conjecture for degree 3 in dimension 3
why: Subsumed by existing 'Keller maps of degree 4' (degree <=4, dimension 3).

title: Prime Nim Grundy growth
why: Same as existing 'Prime Nim values stay small' / 'Unbounded Prime Nim'.

title: Seven-free powers of three
why: Erdos-type digits-of-powers finiteness (like 2^n without ternary digit 2); hopeless with current methods.

title: Primes with digit sum equal to a prime in two bases
why: Essentially existing 'Joint digit sums of primes' (bases 2 and 10), strengthened; joint two-base digit sums of primes open.

title: Treewidth of the prime-sum graph
why: tw<=n via odd vertex cover; mod-3 structure gives C6 blow-up separators so c<1; exact c needs prime sums on dense sets.
